display.title: The Power of Achdus
display.summary_short: Before Rosh Hashanah: why we crown Hashem together in unity, why there is no reason to be angry when everything is from Hashem, and the story of a man who thought he had an anger problem.
display.summary_long: Ahead of Rosh Hashanah, the storyteller explains that besides the shofar we crown Hashem as King, and as the Alter Rebbe teaches from the verse 'Vayehi bi'Yeshurun melech', Hashem is King when all of Israel stands together. What keeps us apart is being upset with someone; it is better to make up first, like everyone in a leaking boat fixing the hole together. Then he teaches that everything except our choice to keep Torah and mitzvos comes from Hashem, so the boy who breaks your pencil is only Hashem's tool, like a carpenter's hammer, and Dovid HaMelech did not punish Shimi ben Gera. The story: Feivel asks his rav for help with his temper. The rav's gabbai spills Feivel's coffee and insults him, and Feivel stays calm because he overheard that it was a test. The rav tells him his real problem is emunah: every challenge is Hashem's test. The storyteller closes with the Rebbe apologizing in a letter to a rav who felt ignored, and Moshe Rabbeinu admitting a mistake, urging everyone to make up during Elul and come to Rosh Hashanah united.
display.lesson: Everything comes from Hashem, so there is no reason to be angry at people; make up with others, even first, and come to Rosh Hashanah united.

sources_cited.note: 'Vayehi bi'Yeshurun melech', brought by the Alter Rebbe.
The Alter Rebbe on crowning Hashem through unity (as cited).
When something bad happens, examine your deeds and do teshuvah.
One who overcomes his anger has his sins forgiven.
The Rebbe's notes and letters: we do not always understand Hashem's ways; the Rebbe's apology to a rav.
Moshe Rabbeinu admits Aharon was right (Parshas Shemini).
